title: 微生物学
subtitle: Microbiology
keywords: Microorganisms 2.Types and cell structure 3.Growth and metabolism 4.Genetic engineering 5.Regional cooperation and environmental protection
educationalGoal: Humans have been producing various fermented foods, such as bread, liquor, cheese, yogurt, and miso, using microorganisms since ancient times. In recent years, microorganisms have become widely used in the fields of pharmaceuticals, environmental protection, waste recycling, material production, and energy in addition to food. Students will learn about the microorganisms and their various applications.
advice: It is important to have basic knowledge of microbiology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology, gene engineering and protein engineering. 1. Microorganisms: culture and observation 2. Types and cell structure: composition of a typical prokaryotic cell 3. Growth and metabolism: ATP production, nutrition and metabolism 4. Genetic engineering: heredity, repair, mutation, and recombinant microorganisms in biotechnology 5. Function of microorganisms: fermentation, medicine, production of useful substances 6. Environmental protection: current environmental protection and initiatives
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of microbiology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology, gene engineering and protein engineering.

activityGoals.body: Ability to explain how to operate laboratory equipment and instruments used to culture microorganisms.
Ability to explain the cell structure, classification, metabolism of a microorganism.
Ability to explain the mutation and transformation of microorganisms.
Ability to explain the effective use of microorganisms, such as environmental protection and energy production.
Ability to explain the relationship between the use of microorganisms and local industries.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1. Systematically explain the type and classification. 2. Explain the structure of a typical prokaryotic cell and eukaryotic cell in detail. 3. Explain mutations with examples. 4. Fully explain the principle of transformation. 5. Explain multiple examples of substance production by microorganisms. 6. Explain drug-resistant bacteria. 7. Fully explain microorganisms involved in material circulation. 8. Fully explain biotechnology for environmental issues.
achievementLevels.standard: 1. Explain the type and classification. 2. Explain the structure of a typical prokaryotic cell and eukaryotic cell. 3. Briefly explain mutation. 4. Briefly explain the principle of transformation. 5. Explain one example of substance production. 6. Explain antibiotics. 7. Explain about microorganisms involved in material circulation. 8. Explain the biotechnology for environmental protection.
